text.p: Tallinna Pank, the fourth largest bank in Estonia, said on Thursday it had started a 440 million kroon financial programme.
The bank will repay some of its old expensive loans, revise interest rates on deposits and extend its loan portfolio, Martti Siimann, director of financial markets, said in a statement.
The bank paid back 15 million kroons to Tallinn city and 30 million kroons to the State Social Office. The loans carried an interest rate of 11 percent.
Next week when the bank will obtain a subordinated loan of 40 million kroons from European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
At the end of May, the bank is due to get part of a 400 million kroon syndicated loan, signed on Monday.
"The syndicated loan should have a positive impact on the liquidity of all Estonia's money market, which has suffered from the growth in loan portfolios," Siimann said.
